new_statements.quote: Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Wörter auf der Pänultima des Grundwortes. [...] Eine dritte Gruppe von Sprachen hat den Ton auf die nunmehrige Pänultima gerückt. Hierher die Sprachen von Paulohi, Batumerah, Sepa, Wolu und die meisten Wemale-Dialekte [...], sowie der östliche Sapalewa-Dialekt. Daher: [...] Vogel SA. mánu'-ě > [...] W. manú'-o [...] [p.176:] Heftet sich dem Verbum ein Personal-Suffix an, so rückt der Ton in den meisten Abkömmlingen des SA. nach dem Wortende, so im Paulohi, den Wemale-Dialekten und dem Wolu, z. B.: Paul. u-tunú-i ich schieße ihn | W. jau a-soli-u ich bade.
new_statements.translation: Proto-Ambon stressed all words of more than one syllable on the penult of the base word. [...] A third group of languages has moved the stress onto what is now the penult [i.e. counting the added support vowel / noun ending]. To this group belong the languages of Paulohi, Batumerah, Sepa, Wolu and most Wemale dialects [...], as well as the eastern Sapalewa dialect. Hence: [...] 'bird' SA. mánu'-ě > [...] W[olu] manú'-o [...] [p.176:] If a personal suffix is attached to the verb, the stress moves toward the end of the word in most descendants of SA., thus in Paulohi, the Wemale dialects and Wolu, e.g. Paul. u-tunú-i 'I shoot him' | W. jau a-soli-u 'I bathe'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: In Wolu (Stresemann's Teluti dialect) stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the whole word: the inherited penult stress is recomputed after the noun ending -o is added (manú'-o, not mánu'-o), the accent likewise shifts when possessive enclitics are added (p.175, unlike Asilulu líma-ku), and it moves rightward when person suffixes attach to verbs (p.176) -- i.e. regular word-penultimate stress including suffixes/enclitics.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Wolu/Sepa. (Within the same group some Wemale dialects 'occasionally still keep the stress on what is now the antepenult'; Hatue and Nuaulu keep stress on the base penult with person suffixes.) The continuation of the p.175 sentence on possessive suffixes ('... haben den Akzent auf die nunmehrige...') was not retrieved in full.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, stated diachronically/comparatively for isolated nouns with the support vowel/noun marker (-o) and for verbs with person suffixes and nouns with possessive enclitics; based on Stresemann's own 1910-12 field recordings, transcribed with acute accents. No phrase-level information.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement concerns 'Wolu', Stresemann's (1927) label for the Teluti dialect recorded at the village of Wolu on Teluti Bay (= West Teluti / 'West Sou Nama' dialect: Haya, Wolu, Tehoru, Tehua; Ethnologue 2019, Loski & Loski 1989:113 fn.17 'Stresemann (1927) refers to the Teluti dialect as Wolu'; Collins 1983:110 'Wolu, a Teluti dialect'). It is grouped with Sepa [spb, sepa1242], the sister dialect of the Sepa-Teluti (East Littoral) language. The language is now called Sou Nama (ISO CR 2015-007). The abbreviation 'W.' in Stresemann's examples is inferred to be Wolu (it directly follows the naming of 'dem Wolu' in both passages); the abbreviation key itself was not retrieved.
